LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we take care of our immediate environment?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions
2. respond to simple questions correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Respond to simple questions correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to simple questions correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to simple questions correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to simple questions correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a partner. (skill: respond to simple questions correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions.
3. Practise this skill: respond to simple questions correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we take care of our immediate environment?
2. Why do we use imitative speaking to learn languages?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use appropriate pronunciation and intonation to describe weather conditions.
5. Be able to: respond to simple questions correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
